newsitem.title: JAPAN: Burger King hopes to take a bite of Japanese market.
newsitem.headline: Burger King hopes to take a bite of Japanese market.

text.p: Fast-food giant Burger King Corp. has taken its time entering Japan, but the company said Thursday it is confident it can still get its teeth into a hefty chunk of the market currently dominated by rival McDonald's Corp.
The world's second-largest hamburger chain spent the past few years probing Japan's $50 billion hamburger market through franchises operated by Seibu Railway Co.
"The test marketing has gone reasonably well," Burger King Chief Executive Officer Robert Lowes told reporters.

The potential of the Japanese market has encouraged the company to form Burger King Japan, a 50-50 joint venture between Japan Tobacco Inc. and Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, which is the parent company of Florida-based Burger King.
David Chapman, Burger King's managing director and vice president for the Asia Pacific, said that for the company's business to take off, at least 200 outlets were needed.
Currently, Burger King is selling its Whopper hamburgers and french fries at five directly owned outlets in Tokyo, which it hopes to expand to 35 by the end of the calendar year, he said.

Archrival McDonald's Co. (Japan) Ltd. has been conducting a fierce price-cutting campaign, slashing hamburger prices to as low as 80 yen (72 cents), but Burger King officials, with their cheapest burger at priced at 220 yen ($2), are not worried.

"What we want to do is to bring the best burger and with value that does not necessarily mean the lowest price," Lowes said. "The Japanese consumer has shown willingess to pay incremental amounts for good quality."

He noted that the Haagen-Dazs ice cream brand was unknown seven years ago, but is now the largest premium brand ice cream in Japan. Haagen-Dazs Japan Inc., which operates ice cream parlours and sells ice cream, is also a member of the GrandMet family.
Burger King officials said their target clientele was mainly young females, ranging between 18 and 23 years of age.
"Japan has a wide variety of food to choose from and a great number of females are attracted to our restaurants," a Burger King Japan marketing manager said.
"In the U.S. it is slightly slanted toward males."
